**🚨 issue (security):** Cookie name should be validated/sanitized to avoid invalid or unsafe header values.

Currently only emptiness is checked; RFC-compliant cookie names must exclude whitespace, semicolons, control characters, etc. This can allow malformed cookies or even header injection if an unsafe name is passed. Please tighten validation (e.g., restrict to token characters) or at least reject `;`, `\r`, `\n`, and spaces.

1\. Set-cookie header injection 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security 
serializeSetCookie interpolates input.name, input.path, and input.domain directly into a
Set-Cookie header value without rejecting CR/LF or delimiter characters, enabling
response-splitting/header-injection if these fields are attacker-controlled. Only input.value is
encoded, and path/domain receive no validation at all.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `serializeSetCookie` builds a `Set-Cookie` header value by concatenating raw `name`, `path`, and `domain` fields. If any of these inputs can be influenced by an attacker, CRLF (or other delimiter characters) can lead to response-splitting / header injection. ## Issue Context Only `value` is encoded; `name`, `path`, and `domain` are inserted verbatim. ## Fix Focus Areas - Add strict validation that rejects `\r`, `\n`, NUL, and cookie delimiter characters (at minimum `;` and `=`) in `name`, and rejects `\r`/`\n`/NUL/`;` in `path` and `domain`. - Consider trimming and validating `name` against a conservative token regex before serialization. - Add focused unit tests that verify CRLF in `name`/`path`/`domain` throws `BadRequestError`. - packages/http/src/cookies.ts[71-103] - packages/http/src/__tests__/cookies.test.ts[1-88] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Store parsed cookies in a null-prototype object**

`parseCookieHeader` writes untrusted cookie names into a plain `{}` map, so special keys like `__proto__` do not behave as normal data keys and can be dropped instead of preserved. In practice, parsing `__proto__=x` yields an object without that cookie entry, which is an incorrect parse result for a valid cookie name and can create prototype-related hazards. Using `Object.create(null)` (or `Map`) avoids this class of key collisions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require auth.mode when asserting HttpRouteMeta**

This validator is declared as `asserts value is HttpRouteMeta`, but it currently accepts `{ auth: {} }` by only rejecting invalid `mode` values when `mode` is present. That contradicts `AuthRouteMeta` where `mode` is required, so downstream code may trust `value.auth.mode` to be defined after assertion and then fail at runtime on inputs that passed validation. The runtime check should enforce presence of `mode` (or the type should make it optional).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Cookie name validation should reject invalid characters.**

The current validation only checks for empty names but doesn't reject names containing characters that are invalid per RFC 6265 (semicolons, equals, spaces, control characters). This could allow malformed or potentially exploitable `Set-Cookie` headers.


<details>
<summary>🛡️ Proposed fix to validate cookie name characters</summary>

```diff
+const COOKIE_NAME_INVALID_CHARS = /[;=\s,]/;
+
 export function serializeSetCookie(input: SetCookieInput): string {
   if (!input.name || input.name.trim().length === 0) {
     throw new BadRequestError('Cookie name is required', 'HTTP_META_INVALID');
   }
+  if (COOKIE_NAME_INVALID_CHARS.test(input.name)) {
+    throw new BadRequestError('Cookie name contains invalid characters', 'HTTP_META_INVALID');
+  }
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@packages/http/src/cookies.ts` around lines 71 - 77, serializeSetCookie
currently only checks for empty cookie names; update it to reject names
containing RFC 6265-disallowed characters (e.g., semicolon ';', comma ',',
whitespace, '=', and control characters). Inside serializeSetCookie, validate
input.name with a character check (or regex) that ensures it contains only
allowed token characters and if it fails throw BadRequestError (same error code
'HTTP_META_INVALID') with a clear message like "Invalid cookie name". Reference
serializeSetCookie and the input.name field when adding this validation so
malformed names are rejected before proceeding to encode the value.
```

</details>

**`SameSite=None` requires `Secure` flag** Per [RFC 6265bis](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis) and modern browser policy (Chrome 80+, Firefox 79+), a cookie with `SameSite=None` **must** also carry the `Secure` attribute — otherwise browsers will either reject the cookie entirely or silently downgrade it to `SameSite=Lax`. The current code allows `{ sameSite: 'none', secure: false }`, which produces `SameSite=None` without `Secure` — a spec-invalid header that will be silently dropped by all modern browsers. The `normalizeSameSite` call happens before the `Secure` check, so there is no guard against this combination. A validation check should be added after the SameSite value is resolved: ``` const sameSite = normalizeSameSite(input.sameSite); const isSecure = input.secure ?? true; if (sameSite === 'none' && !isSecure) { throw new BadRequestError( 'SameSite=None cookies must also set Secure', 'HTTP_META_INVALID' ); } const parts = [`${input.name}=${encodeURIComponent(input.value)}`]; ```

**Runtime validator allows `mode` absent despite required type** `AuthRouteMeta` declares `mode` as a required field (`mode: 'none' | 'cookie-session' | 'bearer' | 'hybrid'`), but the runtime guard treats it as optional — objects missing `mode` entirely pass `assertValidRouteMeta` successfully. This creates a type/runtime mismatch: a caller passing `{ auth: {} }` gets a clean assertion cast to `HttpRouteMeta`, yet any downstream code expecting `meta.auth.mode` to be defined will encounter `undefined` at runtime. ```typescript const mode = value.auth.mode; if (mode !== undefined && !['none', 'cookie-session', 'bearer', 'hybrid'].includes(String(mode))) { ``` Consider making the `mode` check unconditional when `auth` is present, or changing the `AuthRouteMeta` type to make `mode` optional.

**Fragile error-case test pattern** Both error-path tests (lines 24-38 and 73-86) use a raw `try/catch` with a sentinel `throw` inside the `try` block. If the expected error is NOT thrown, the sentinel error (`new Error('Expected invalid sameSite error')`) will be caught by the `catch` block and the `toMatchObject` assertion will fail — but the failure message will be about a property mismatch rather than the clear "this should have thrown" intent. Vitest's built-in `.toThrow()` matcher communicates intent more clearly and produces better error messages: ```typescript it('rejects invalid sameSite values with HTTP_META_INVALID', () => { expect(() => serializeSetCookie({ name: 'bad-cookie', value: 'x', sameSite: 'invalid' as never, }) ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ name: 'BadRequestError', code: 'HTTP_META_INVALID', statusCode: 400, })); }); ``` The same pattern applies to the `assertValidRouteMeta` error case at lines 73-86.
